_meta.legal_basis: Indian Contract Act 1872 + Sale of Goods Act 1930 + Competition Act 2002
_meta.notes: Distribution / Dealership Agreement. Hard exclusivity, resale price maintenance, territorial restrictions may face Competition Act 2002 S.3 scrutiny (anti-competitive agreements). CCI has examined exclusive distribution arrangements - Schott Glass India case. Permitted only if no AAEC. RPM is per se anti-competitive in India.

title: Distribution / Dealership Agreement

enum: Sole (Supplier may sell but no other distributor)

mandatory_clauses.title: Territory and Exclusivity
mandatory_clauses.note: Competition Act 2002 S.3 - exclusivity must not cause appreciable adverse effect on competition (AAEC). Avoid absolute territorial protection.

mandatory_clauses.title: Orders, Supply, Delivery, Risk and Title
mandatory_clauses.statutory_basis: Sale of Goods Act 1930 S.18-25 (transfer of property)

mandatory_clauses.title: Prices, Discounts, Margin, GST
mandatory_clauses.note: Avoid Resale Price Maintenance (RPM) - per se anti-competitive under S.3(4)(e). MRP may be communicated but not enforced as minimum resale price.

mandatory_clauses.title: Trademark and Branding License
mandatory_clauses.content: Supplier grants Distributor a non-exclusive, revocable license to use Supplier's trademarks solely for the purpose of marketing and selling the Products in the Territory during the Term. All goodwill accrues to Supplier.

mandatory_clauses.title: Distributor's Obligations
subclauses: No sale outside Territory (subject to passive sales permitted under Comp Act)

mandatory_clauses.title: Compliance with Laws (anti-bribery, FCPA-equivalent, Consumer Protection)
Non-Compete (Restraint of Trade Compliance)
mandatory_clauses.note: In-term non-compete typically valid. Post-term restraint must be reasonable and limited - S.27 caution.

prompt_context.system_role: You are drafting a Distribution/Dealership Agreement under Indian law. Watch out for Competition Act 2002 S.3 issues - avoid RPM, absolute territorial restrictions, refusal to deal where market power exists.
drafting_rules: Exclusivity: structure as territorial appointment, not absolute restraint on passive sales. CCI permits exclusive distribution if no AAEC.
Pricing: do NOT include RPM (minimum resale prices). MRP can be communicated but not enforced. RPM is per se violation under S.3(4)(e).
Tie-in / refusal to deal / bundling - avoid unless justified.
Trademark license is non-exclusive, revocable, with goodwill to Supplier.
Sale of Goods Act S.18-25 for property and risk transfer.
Minimum off-take with consequences for non-achievement (price increase, loss of exclusivity, termination).
Termination compensation: Indian law does not mandate distributor termination compensation, but contract should be clear.

filing_checklist: Execute on stamp paper per state.
Verify GST registration of both parties.
Register trademark license with TM Registry if applicable (S.49 TM Act).
Cross-border: comply with FEMA, RBI reporting, Customs.

validation_rules.check: No clause fixing minimum resale price
Passive sales not prohibited if exclusivity granted
TM license clause with goodwill to Supplier
